item.description: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images Micah Parsons has finally made his long-awaited return to the field following his season-ending injury last year, but fans are not convinced he looks right after footage was shared on Thursday. The Green Bay Packers take on the New England Patriots this weekend in Foxborough, with Parsons eyeing the Thanksgiving game against the Los Angeles Rams as his comeback. However, it would seem as if there is still a lot of work for Parsons to get on with if he is to make a strong return to the roster. Parsons is returning from a torn ACL and torn meniscus, which has kept him out of the game since December of last year. Although Patrick Mahomes recovered much quicker from his knee injury, Parsons’ journey has not been as straightforward. As his 21-day practice window has now been opened by the Packers, fans have been left far from convinced over the early footage they have seen of Parsons back on the grass at the training facility. NFL fans are not convinced by Micah Parsons’ return to the Packers’ practice Footage was shared from the Packers’ training facility on Thursday of Parsons back in pads and working with the other defenders. However, some fans felt as if they spotted the 27-year-old limping after one of his reps while working with the trainers. ‘Y’all Packers fans coping in the comments.. This doesn’t look promising,’ replied one NFL fan on X. ‘Left leg doesn’t look right,’ added another. Parsons was wearing a brace on his left knee, which is to be expected of a player making their return from such an injury. item.title: Carmelo Anthony names who he thinks is the MVP in the NBA so far this season
item.description: Photo by Erica Denhoff/NurPhoto via Getty Images Former NBA star Carmelo Anthony has named his early pick for MVP. Carmelo Anthony has become the latest big name to support Luka Doncic’s impressive early march towards the MVP Award. Luka Doncic is averaging a staggering 38.5 points per game this season, with 40 points or more in each of his last three games. The Slovenian’s form has led the Lakers to second place in the Western Conference, with a 7-2 overall record. Speaking to 7PM In Brooklyn , Carmelo Anthony picked out Doncic when he was asked to name his choice for MVP. He responded: “I would have to go with Luka at this point. If you get a healthy Luka, an in shape Luka, a focused Luka, giving effort on the defensive end Luka, committing to that part of it, that is a different Luka right there. “If that is sustainable we’re talking about the West a lot differently. “His level of play and focus and determination, you can see it in his bounce, he is driving, switching hands, getting and ones and yelling. That’s a different Luka right there.” Doncic has also earned praise for his defensive play this season, an area where he has been heavily criticized in the past. MVP race wide open For the last two seasons, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has won the MVP. But his task with the Oklahoma City Thunder is far tougher this season. The Thunder have lost Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren to long-term injuries. SGA showed he has still got what it takes, with two 40+ performances in back-to-back wins over the Cavaliers. His season average is 30.1, a dip on his previous two seasons. OKC’s record is 6-2 for the season so far. The other factor in play is voter fatigue. Doncic’s offensive explosion is more eye-catching and more exciting, and the story of him winning his first MVP Award the year after LeBron James left the Lakers is an engaging narrative. item.title: Permane to stay as Racing Bulls team principal
item.description: Alan Permane has been at Racing Bulls since the start of 2024 [Getty Images] Red Bull have extended Alan Permane's contract as boss of their second team until the end of 2031. The 59-year-old Englishman was promoted from racing director to team principal of Racing Bulls in July 2025, when predecessor Laurent Mekies was moved to the same role at Red Bull following the sacking of Christian Horner. The team secured their first podium finish in four years at last season's Dutch Grand Prix with Isack Hadjar, and this season are fifth in the championship - the leading outfit behind the 'big four' - after 19 races. Oliver Mintzlaff, who runs Red Bull's F1 programme as chief executive officer of corporate projects and investments, said: "Alan is doing a tremendous job, and the progress the team has made is a direct reflection of his experience, commitment and competitive mindset. "He brings clarity, composure, and a deep understanding of what it takes to perform in Formula 1, while creating an environment where people can consistently deliver at their best. "The results Racing Bulls has achieved in recent seasons underline the strength of the team and the work being done throughout the organisation. "Alan has played a key role in that progress, and we are very pleased that he will continue to lead the team as we look to build on this momentum in the years ahead." Before joining Red Bull, Permane spent 34 years at the team based in Enstone in Oxfordshire through various guises as Benetton, Renault and Lotus, winning two world titles each with Michael Schumacher and Fernando Alonso. He said: "I am immensely proud to be continuing this journey and I would like to thank everyone at Red Bull for the trust and support they have given me. "What makes this team special is the shared spirit of everyone; trackside, in Faenza and in Milton Keynes, and it is a privilege to lead such a talented and committed group every day. "Fighting for fifth in the championship is something we should all be very proud of, but it is the result of years of hard work from a lot of people, and we are not done yet. "We have the right people, the right culture and a clear sense of where we want to go, and I am excited to keep pushing together." "When you talk about defense, you just gotta take away their best threat," Dolphins defensive coordinator Sean Duggan said, adding, "When it comes to Detroit, they have good players everywhere." The Lions have elite talent at quarterback ( Jared Goff ), running back ( Jahmyr Gibbs ), receiver ( Amon-Ra St. Brown ), tight end ( Sam LaPorta ) and offensive line ( Penei Sewell ). item.title: Juventus and Jeep®: partnership honoured at the Global Football Industry Awards
item.description: Juventus and Jeep®: partnership honoured at the Global Football Industry Awards The partnership between Juventus and Jeep® has won the ‘Best Sponsorship or Partnership’ award in London at the 2026 Global Football Industry Awards, which recognise excellence and innovation in the football industry. This accolade celebrates the value of a relationship built over time and follows the Sustainable Game Award won by the Club at the previous edition for its ‘Black, White & More’ ESG strategy. At the heart of the award is a collaboration that began in 2012 and was recently renewed until 2028, having become one of the longest-standing and most recognisable commercial partnerships in European football. This relationship has gone beyond the scope of shirt sponsorship, evolving into an international strategic platform and a defining feature of both brands’ identities. At the heart of this partnership lies a strong shared set of values: performance, ambition, resilience and the determination to constantly push the boundaries. Juventus and Jeep are also united by their connection to Turin, a city where footballing tradition and motoring history converge. Over the years, Jeep has become part of the Bianconeri universe, supporting the men’s and women’s first teams and Juventus Next Gen, as well as all the youth teams, creating campaigns, digital content and initiatives dedicated to the fans. This shared journey has coincided with the winning of 35 trophies and Jeep’s strong commercial growth in Europe. Italy has become the brand’s main market on the continent, with Jeep among the leading brands in the country’s SUV segment. A partnership capable of reinventing itself through creativity: from the reinterpretation of the Jeep logo on the 2022/23 season shirt – featuring lightning-inspired graphics to highlight the brand’s electric vehicles – to the Juventus Summer Tour powered by Jeep, which has taken this collaboration to international markets, from the United States and Canada to Indonesia, South Korea, China, Hong Kong and Australia. These initiatives have transformed the sponsorship into a storytelling tool, creating new opportunities to engage with an international community of fans. The award thus recognises the ability to grow together over time, whilst maintaining a strong strategic focus and nurturing the partnership with new ideas, content and ways of engaging fans. Juventus and Jeep continue to look in the same direction, united by their determination to tackle the challenges ahead and to go further, together.

item.title: Wolves legend and ex-England defender Coady retires
item.description: Conor Coady made 317 of his 503 club appearances in a Wolves shirt [Shutterstock] Wolverhampton Wanderers legend Conor Coady has retired from playing at the age of 33. The former Wolves skipper, who won 10 England caps, has been linked with a move into coaching, having been without a club since leaving Wrexham in September. After beginning as a promising midfielder in the Liverpool academy, where he was compared in some quarters to Steven Gerrard, he moved first on loan to Sheffield United in 2013, before signing for Huddersfield Town at the end of that season. But he enjoyed most of his success at Wolves after being converted into a central defender by then boss Nuno Espirito Santo. He also played for Everton, Leicester City, Wrexham and on loan at Charlton last season in his 503-game club career. Coady was signed by then Wolves boss Kenny Jackett in 2015 - and played a major part in the club's promotion back to the Premier League in 2018. He captained the Wolves team who twice finished seventh and also reached the quarter-finals of the Europa League. In all, he made 317 Wolves appearances, scoring seven of his career tally - for club and country - of 22 goals, before being allowed to leave on loan for Everton in 2022. He then joined Leicester for a reported £8.5m in July 2023 after Everton opted not to complete a £4.5m deal to turn his season-long loan into a permanent switch. Coady, who works as a pundit for BBC Radio 5 Live, then moved on to an ill-fated short spell at Wrexham , which was ended prematurely before his final move to The Valley , to join Nathan Jones' Charlton. item.title: Big Ten Tournament semifinals preview: No. 2-seed Maryland field hockey vs. No. 6-seed Iowa
item.description: No. 2-seed Maryland field hockey (17-1, 7-1 Big Ten) concluded the regular season as the Big Ten’s best offense. No. 6-seed Iowa (13-4, 4-4 Big Ten) features the conference’s top two goalscorers. The last time these two sides squared off, six combined goals were scored. Maryland and Iowa will play this Friday afternoon at 4 p.m. in Columbus, Ohio with the winner advancing to the Big Ten Tournament final. The game will be televised on the Big Ten Network. What happened last time Last Friday, then-No. 2 Maryland welcomed then-No. 9 Iowa to College Park for a late-October clash to wrap up the regular season. What ensued was a bloodbath, as the Terps handed the Hawkeyes their worst loss of the season, 5-1. The Terps stormed out of the gates, tallying three goals within the first 15 minutes. Maci Bradford got the party started before 90 seconds had elapsed, and Francisca Eschoyez buried a pair of penalty-corner lasers to stretch the lead. After a quiet second quarter, the Terps went back to work in the third period. Both Bradford and Ella Beach found the scoresheet with set-piece goals. The Terps smoked the Hawkeyes in the penalty corner department. Maryland had eight corners and scored four times, while Iowa forced just three corners and scored only once. Last Friday was a career day for Bradford, as the senior collected a pair of goals and added a pair of assists. Her four-goal involvement tied a career-high set earlier this season. What’s happened since Each team has only played once since last Friday’s bout. Maryland began its Big Ten Tournament run with a 3-1 victory over No. 7-seed Ohio State. The Terps used a two-goal first period to build a quick advantage over the host Buckeyes and held on the rest of the way to ensure the win. On the other side, Iowa upset the red-hot No. 3-seed Penn State in comeback fashion. Like the previous meeting against the Terps, the Hawkeyes fell behind immediately, surrendering a score within the first six minutes. After winning the Le Mans 24 Hours on three consecutive occasions between 2023-25, the Prancing Horse had to settle for a fifth-place finish this time around. In fact, Ferrari has scored just one victory so far in 2026 - a result it inherited after the race-leading #7 Toyota TR010 retired in the final hour due to mechanical gremlins. Ahead of this weekend's season finale at Monza, Ferrari's technical director Ferdinando Cannizzo reviewed the team's campaign while also crediting Toyota, which has returned to top form this year with the introduction of a revised car. "Toyota has always proved to be a very strong team. Perhaps last year they took a little holiday... "I think they probably didn't expect Ferrari to be so strong right from its first season. They were caught a little off guard by that initially, but then they bounced back very well. This year they really gave us a hard time and were competitive throughout the entire season. "I imagine that revisiting certain areas of the car also helped them, giving them a significant boost. I'd like to congratulate them once again because they have done a really good job. They have made virtually no mistakes throughout the season, so they certainly deserve what they have achieved this year. "We can see that we have done a good job this year. Mandatory Credit: Chris Carter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It took until the second half, but Louisville started to get more aggressive with their linebackers. On this play, Stanquan Clark times up the snap before shooting the gap to make a play in the backfield. He’s just unlucky because the play goes to the other side, which leaves him grasping for air. Stanford uses motion again on this play with a full shift of their tight ends across the field. Louisville tracks the motion, but you will notice that no one picks up the running back coming out of the backfield. So, on this play, Stanford takes advantage of two different issues UofL had in coverage earlier in the game. They don’t identify their responsibility after the motion, and they don’t account for the running back out of the backfield on a short-yardage pass. This is a nice play design and call by Stanford, but it would be nice to be able to say that the play just beat Louisville as opposed to the defense not even giving itself a chance. Lincoln Kienholz had his weekly instalment of “Man, it’s nice to have a quarterback who can do this” in the second quarter with his arm, but he does it with his legs on this play. I especially love the spin move that wasn’t really needed. I wrote about Louisville needing to attack the edges of Stanford’s defense in the What To Watch For post last week, so I was really happy to see them try to get outside a lot in this game. The first drive of the game was edge runs and swing passes, and they came back to it in the third quarter for this nice touchdown. As good as Isaac Brown is in space, he should buy dinner for Jaleel Skinner and TJ McWilliams for their blocking on this play. McWilliams is the outside receiver to the top of the screen. He gets up to the outside linebacker, who is flowing towards him before passing him off to Skinner, who gets outside after going in motion. McWilliams then moves up to the cornerback to create a tunnel for Isaac to run through. This is teach tape. I’m a bit of a broken record on this, but I don’t really understand why they can run this defense as often as they run Cover 3. Situations will dictate a lot of things, but the only real difference is that they are a little more spread out. But if this were first down, you would not be blitzing Kaleb Perry, who loops around on a stunt on this play. He would be right in the middle of the field to play the run. Ben Perry would also not be in press coverage in the slot. He would be backed off a bit and could react to a run play. If they were playing well in zone coverage, this wouldn’t be a problem, but at this point in the season I can’t understand why they haven’t adjusted. item.description: Danks offers Bayern squad update and discusses potential changes for Mainz clash Still in charge in Vincent Kompany's absence, Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks gave an update on his squad ahead of Saturday's Bundesliga clash with Mainz during a press conference on Friday. Danks revealed that Jamal Musiala and Aleksandar Pavlovic have both returned from injury to train with the team ahead of the game. “Most players trained yesterday. Jamal Musiala has re-joined the group, which is very positive. But tomorrow's game comes too soon for him. Aleks Pavlovic was also involved. We need to see how his legs react. Manuel Neuer trained again. Things look good there for the game,” Danks said. Asked about Musiala and Luis Diaz, who is also progressing in his recovery from injury, Danks said: "I think it's tough to set a date or game for their return. Next week they'll train individually and then be in full team training when everyone's back from the national teams. But there's no deadline." The Bayern assistant coach also revealed that some players could be rested, with Alphonso Davies among those who may need a break amid a congested schedule. “With a few players we need to look at workload and whether we rest them. item.description: Sinner (left), with Cahill, has not played since winning Wimbledon in July [Getty Images] The coach who helped guide Jannik Sinner to five Grand Slam titles and the world number one spot is to leave the player's camp at the end of the year. Australian Darren Cahill, 61, joined the Italian's team in June 2022 when Sinner was just outside the world's top 10 and had never progressed beyond the quarter-finals of a Grand Slam tournament. But, together with Italian coach Simone Vagnozzi, Cahill has helped Sinner to go on to win five Slams and occupy the world number one spot for 95 weeks. Injury has meant the 25-year-old has not played since winning Wimbledon for the second year in a row in July, which led to Alexander Zverev recently overtaking him at the top of the rankings. He is set to return to action at the Six Kings Slam tournament in Saudi Arabia next month. Swede Magnus Norman, the long-time coach of recently retired Stan Wawrinka, will join Sinner's team for next season. "Darren has been an incredibly important part of my journey," Sinner said. "Together with Simone and the whole team, we have achieved things I dreamed of growing up. "He has helped me grow both as a player and as a person, and his guidance will stay with me throughout my career." Cahill had originally planned to leave at the end of 2025, but told Sinner at Wimbledon that the Italian could decide whether he stayed on - as long as he won the title. "Working with Jannik has been a special honour and privilege," Cahill said. item.title: Ex-PSG star Diallo to stand trial for alleged assault on team-mate
item.description: Aminata Diallo (L) is accused of involvement in the attack on her ex-Paris Saint-Germain teammate Kheira Hamraoui (JAVIER SORIANO) Former Paris Saint-Germain women's star Aminata Diallo is to stand trial on charges relating to the assault on her ex-teammate in 2021, according to a court order issued Friday and seen by AFP. Diallo, 31, is believed by the investigating magistrate to have ordered the attack on her fellow former French international teammate and guided the attackers to where the assault took place. She is charged with complicity in violence and criminal conspiracy. Six others will go on trial alongside her. The date for the trial has yet to be announced. In November 2021, Hamraoui was attacked by two masked men, who hit her on her knees with iron bars, after returning from a team dinner in a car with Diallo. "After five long years of the case being investigated, it is a huge relief they have reached a conclusion and soon there will be a trial," Hamraoui's lawyers Julia Minkowski and Said Harir told AFP in a statement. "The whole truth will finally come out in this violent affair which is so rare in football, indeed sport, in which the victim was subjected to an unconscionable campaign of harassment following the assault." Diallo's defence team claimed there had been a lack of fairness in the investigation. "There has neither been a punishment nor questions posed about the methods used in the investigation regarding Aminata Diallo, which is also peppered with false statements," said Romain Ruiz, one of her four-lawyer defence team. "It's as if she has been crying in the desert for four years. We will call out her innocence till the final day of her trial." Hamraoui, 36, lost when she took PSG to a labour court last year claiming damages of 3.5 million-euro ($4m) alleging she was forced out of the club following the assault. Hamraoui was seeking damages from her former club, alleging a lack of support. She claimed she was "ostracised" on the pitch, in the changing room and suffered harassment on social media. item.title: McIlroy fires 63 to move into Abu Dhabi contention
item.description: Rory McIlroy is chasing a sixth successive Race to Dubai crown [Getty Images] Rory McIlroy put the setback of the two-shot penalty he received on Thursday behind him as he posted 11 birdies in shooting a nine-under-par second-round 63 at the Abu Dhabi Championship on Friday. McIlroy had been handed the sanction for improving his lie during the opening round and as a result finished day one on two under par, eight shots behind the leader, Italian Francesco Laporta. The six-time major winner was penalised after pressing down on the grass behind his ball with his club before hitting a chip on the par-four 12th at Yas Links. The Northern Ireland player responded in style in round two however to move to 11 under and assume the clubhouse lead with several of the leading players on the leaderboard still to complete their second 18 holes. McIlroy began his round with a bogey at the first but bounced back by picking up shots at the second, fourth and seventh holes. The back-to-back Masters champion then stormed up the leaderboard with five consecutive birdies from holes nine to 13. A dropped shot at the 14th proved to be only a temporary blip as he recorded two further birdies on the 17th and 18th holes to cap a scintillating round. It isthe first time in his career that he has made 11 birdies in a single round of a DP World Tour event. The 37-year-old is chasing a fifth Race to Dubai title in a row and a record-equalling eighth in total, that would draw him level with Scotland's Colin Montgomerie. McIlroy went into the Abu Dhabi tournament in third position in the standings, behind leader Eugenio Chacarra and second-placed Patrick Reed. American Reed was the long-time Race to Dubai leader after his Rolex Series victory in Dubai and win in Qatar but was recently overtaken as Spaniard Chacarra claimed a third triumph of the season at the DP World India Championship. Chacarra shot a second-round 71 on Friday to sit well down the field on three under, while Reed registered the same score to lie further back on one over. The top 70 available players from the Race to Dubai rankings are competing in Abu Dhabi, with the top 50 progressing to next week's season-ending DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.

item.description: Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images The New York Knicks saw their fair share of celebrities between opening night and their NBA championship run, and two of the stars have lightly called out Taylor Swift. One thing that the New York Knicks winning the NBA championship did for the NBA is bring the celebrities out in full force. The Knicks have some of the most famous fans in the country. Names like Timothee Chalamet, Ben Stiller, and Mariska Hargitay were seen courtside throughout their entire run. Arguably one of the biggest musical stars in the world, Taylor Swift, also made a few appearances to root for the team during the run. However, Enrique is incredibly keen to manage his workload to prevent long-term fatigue. Club release official statement on absence The decision to sideline the Moroccan defender was not made solely by the manager. It was a calculated move agreed upon by the entire sporting hierarchy at the club to protect their star asset. PSG released an official update to clarify the situation and ensure there was no unwanted speculation surrounding the player's sudden absence from the matchday squad. The club's statement read: "In agreement with the coach and the Sporting Direction, Achraf Hakimi is benefiting from a rest period until the start of the international break." Enrique considers his tactical replacement options With Hakimi completely unavailable for the weekend clash, Enrique must find a temporary solution on the right side of his defence. The manager has a few intriguing options at his disposal to step into the role. Warren Zaire-Emery could be asked to fill in at right-back against Troyes. The versatile midfielder has already made nine league appearances this season and possesses the tactical intelligence to adapt to a defensive assignment. Alternatively, Enrique could turn to the club's youth academy. Highly-rated 17-year-old David Boly, who has made one Ligue 1 appearance so far, is also in contention to start the match. Upcoming fixtures and international return dates The Parisiens will look to secure three points against Troyes on Saturday without their star right-back. The Parisian outfit are eager to maintain their strong form in domestic competition and build momentum. Following the weekend fixture, domestic football will pause for the international window. Hakimi is expected to link up with the Morocco national team for their upcoming fixtures, assuming he is selected for duty.
